title: Cracks Beneath the AI Boom: Is the U.S. Economy Heading For a Downturn? | The Weekly Wrap
summary: The November 7 wrap connects narrow equity leadership with a divided economy, reviews AI expectations and warns that expensive stocks need more than merely good results. It also revisits FICO competition and explains banking money creation.
assessment: His warnings about valuation expectations and product differentiation are useful. The no-sales-force Palantir description is false, and the money-creation lesson conflates deposits, capital and reserves. Equity-index concentration is observable but does not itself prove that the rest of the economy has stopped growing.
framework_points: Distinguish operating growth from what the valuation requires.
Avoid shorting solely because a successful company is expensive.
Prefer differentiated products over easily substituted hardware.
transcript_cautions: The stated Monday November 4 date is inconsistent with the 2025 calendar; no investment verdict rests on the weekday slip.
The no-sales-force claim is adopted from Dan Ives and explicitly attributed as such.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Cooling labor conditions and concentrated affluent spending make the economy vulnerable to a stock-market correction.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track real spending by income, employment and wealth sensitivity.
claims.reason: The vulnerability is conditional, and the reported top-decile spending share needs a defined dataset. Distributional stress does not itself establish an imminent recession.
claims.next_check: Track real spending by income, employment and wealth sensitivity.

claims.claim: Equal-weight indexes reveal market participation concealed by megacap weights.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use matching total-return series and rebalance conventions.
claims.reason: A capitalization-weighted average and an equally weighted average answer different questions. The return gap measures dispersion in contributions, subject to rebalancing.
claims.next_check: Use matching total-return series and rebalance conventions.

assumptions: Use the same constituent universe and time interval.
proof.proof: Cap weighting gives more influence to larger initial weights; equal weighting assigns equal initial weights. Their return difference reveals the effect of weighting, not directly the GDP contribution of each firm.
proof.derivation: Cap weighting gives more influence to larger initial weights; equal weighting assigns equal initial weights. Their return difference reveals the effect of weighting, not directly the GDP contribution of each firm.

claims.claim: A return gap worse than the recent roughly ten-percentage-point norm should trigger greater concern.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Test the threshold against future drawdown and earnings breadth.
claims.reason: The rule has no precise forward-risk measure or horizon and is not calibrated as a forecasting model.
claims.next_check: Test the threshold against future drawdown and earnings breadth.

claims.claim: Top-heavy index performance proves a K-shaped real economy.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare market concentration with independent employment, spending and GDP data.
claims.reason: It demonstrates stock-market concentration; firms listed in the index and their weights do not map directly to household incomes or domestic value added.
claims.next_check: Compare market concentration with independent employment, spending and GDP data.

assumptions: Market capitalization reflects expected global equity cash flows, not current domestic output.
proof.proof: An index can become concentrated through valuation changes without a corresponding shift in current household income or GDP. Therefore market concentration alone cannot prove a particular real-economy distribution.
proof.derivation: An index can become concentrated through valuation changes without a corresponding shift in current household income or GDP. Therefore market concentration alone cannot prove a particular real-economy distribution.

claims.claim: A Mamdani administration may hurt New York property and encourage business relocation.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track enacted policies, rents, employment and net relocations.
claims.reason: He flags potential consequences rather than a dated net-outflow prediction. A flat election-day stock response is not proof that all costs were already priced.
claims.next_check: Track enacted policies, rents, employment and net relocations.

claims.claim: AI earnings growth remains strong but analysts have caught up, making beats less powerful for stocks.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare forecast errors, estimate revisions and valuation across releases.
claims.reason: This requires a consistent surprise and revision dataset rather than selected reports.
claims.next_check: Compare forecast errors, estimate revisions and valuation across releases.

claims.claim: Palantir has no sales force and obtains every sale through word of mouth.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Read sales practices and selling expense disclosures.
claims.reason: The pre-episode filing explicitly describes its direct sales force and sales organization. The adopted guest explanation overstates organic distribution.

evidence.title: Palantir Q2 2025 filing
evidence.finding: The filing explicitly describes a direct sales force and efforts to build sales operations. Word of mouth and bootcamps do not mean the company has no sales force.

claims.next_check: Read sales practices and selling expense disclosures.

claims.claim: Palantir analyzes customer data better than customers can, and MongoDB does the same thing less effectively.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare use cases, deployment cost, measurable outcomes and competing products.
claims.reason: The explanation needs product-specific comparisons; data platforms and databases are not interchangeable in every workflow. Reported customer anecdotes do not establish universal superiority.
claims.next_check: Compare use cases, deployment cost, measurable outcomes and competing products.

claims.claim: Shorting a strong company solely on valuation is dangerous; he has no Palantir position.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define catalyst, borrow costs, loss limits and time horizon.
claims.reason: This is his risk-management preference and disclosure, not a forecast that the stock cannot fall. He does not independently verify the full Burry thesis.
claims.next_check: Define catalyst, borrow costs, loss limits and time horizon.

claims.claim: AMD and Arista can deliver growth yet disappoint when forward margins or guidance merely meet high expectations.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate operating performance, forecasts and the valuation embedded before release.
claims.reason: The expectations mechanism is plausible, but a single price reaction does not identify all causes.
claims.next_check: Separate operating performance, forecasts and the valuation embedded before release.

claims.claim: Commodity-like server products expose Super Micro and Dell to price and margin pressure despite AI demand.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare gross margins, system features, customer concentration and capacity.
claims.reason: Differentiation, execution, mix and accounting issues can all affect margins. The degree of commoditization needs actual competing configurations and pricing.
claims.next_check: Compare gross margins, system features, customer concentration and capacity.

claims.claim: Eaton illustrates that AI-related industrials can still miss expectations after a valuation re-rating.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track organic growth, margin, order trends and beginning multiples.
claims.reason: This is a valuation-risk illustration, not a prediction of permanent business impairment.
claims.next_check: Track organic growth, margin, order trends and beginning multiples.

claims.claim: Gartner remains under pressure from federal consulting cuts and fear of AI substitution despite improved guidance.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare contract value, renewal rates, public-sector exposure and AI products.
claims.reason: Fear is distinct from realized customer replacement. The stock move does not establish the actual share of business lost to AI.
claims.next_check: Compare contract value, renewal rates, public-sector exposure and AI products.

claims.claim: Uber must eventually adapt to autonomous driving, though the transition is not yet complete.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Model ride supply, fleet ownership, take rates and partnership economics.
claims.reason: No adoption or earnings horizon is specified. Partnerships could alter the outcome.
claims.next_check: Model ride supply, fleet ownership, take rates and partnership economics.

claims.claim: PJT strong advisory results support the current M&A-cycle thesis.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare advisory revenue, backlog, compensation and completed transactions.
claims.reason: The specific quarter was not independently inspected here. Advisory strength need not establish every part of a future broad deal wave or a stock target.
claims.next_check: Compare advisory revenue, backlog, compensation and completed transactions.

claims.claim: Fee-related earnings provide a steadier basis for asset-manager valuation than realization-dependent profits, while private-credit risks emerge in downturns.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate recurring fees, investment performance, fundraising and credit losses.
claims.reason: Fee stability depends on asset bases, redemptions and contracts; it is not risk-free. The recession warning has no date.
claims.next_check: Separate recurring fees, investment performance, fundraising and credit losses.

claims.claim: Restaurant weakness reveals stress among lower- and middle-income consumers despite healthy aggregate payment volume.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare income cohorts, traffic, pricing and market share.
claims.reason: Restaurant-specific competition and younger-customer exposure are not identical to low income. Aggregate volume can coexist with subgroup stress, but this needs direct data.
claims.next_check: Compare income cohorts, traffic, pricing and market share.

claims.claim: Lilly is gaining at Novo Nordisk expense in obesity drugs.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track volume, net prices, capacity and indication-specific market share.
claims.reason: Repeated guidance cuts suggest pressure but the causal share shift requires matched prescription and price evidence.
claims.next_check: Track volume, net prices, capacity and indication-specific market share.

claims.claim: Trex and CarMax weakness show housing and used-auto pressure beyond the AI boom.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track volumes, inventory, pricing, competition and credit costs.
claims.reason: The contemporary diagnoses require issuer releases and cannot by themselves establish future collapse of both industries.
claims.next_check: Track volumes, inventory, pricing, competition and credit costs.

claims.claim: FICO aggressive pricing invites a dangerous challenge from suppliers that also own VantageScore.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track funded-loan adoption and revenue under competing price structures.
claims.reason: The strategic conflict is real as a mechanism, but the financial effect depends on lender choice, implementation and licensing terms. Betting the company is not a quantified insolvency forecast.
claims.next_check: Track funded-loan adoption and revenue under competing price structures.

claims.claim: A bank keeps roughly 10% of a deposit as capital or liquidity and repeatedly relends the rest to create money.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Follow loan/deposit balance-sheet entries and separate capital, liquidity and settlement constraints.
claims.reason: This conflates capital, reserves and liquidity. US transaction reserve requirements were zero, and modern lending creates a matching deposit rather than mechanically multiplying a prior deposit under a 10% rule.

evidence.title: Reserve requirements
evidence.finding: Transaction-account reserve requirements were reduced to zero in March 2020. Capital and liquidity constraints remain separate requirements.

evidence.title: Money creation in the modern economy
evidence.finding: Bank lending creates a matching deposit; banks do not simply lend out a fixed fraction of prior deposits under a mechanical money multiplier. Profitability, capital, liquidity and monetary policy constrain lending.

claims.next_check: Follow loan/deposit balance-sheet entries and separate capital, liquidity and settlement constraints.
